title: Permissioning + internal feature flag for Unit Economics dashboard (RBAC + audit logging)
creator: Chloe Martin
description:
## Context
The Unit Economics dashboard is internal-only in v1 and includes sensitive cost and margin-adjacent signals (GPU rate card applications, blended $/1M output tokens, allocation knobs). We need:
1) a feature flag to hard-gate access at runtime
2) RBAC permission checks for API + UI routes
3) audit logging for access + permission changes (and optionally “view” events)

This ticket covers Console + backend permissioning patterns and required audit events. It does *not* cover data redaction rules inside results (separate work) or external/customer access.

## Requirements
### Feature flag
- Flag name: `unit_econ_dashboard_internal`
- Default: OFF for all users (safe default)
- Enablement: allowlist by group (Finance, Product, Platform Eng) during dogfood; later broaden to “All employees” once data quality + comms are ready.
- Enforcement points:
  - Console UI: route guard (hide nav item; direct URL should show permission denied)
  - Backend: deny requests when flag is OFF, even if RBAC allows

### RBAC
- New permission(s):
  - `console.unit_economics.view_internal`
  - (optional, if needed for future) `console.unit_economics.admin` (manage saved views / configuration)
- Protect:
  - API endpoints introduced in ENG-8427 (time series + breakdowns)
  - Any export endpoints / reconciliation report links surfaced in UI
- Denial behavior:
  - 403 with stable error code `UNIT_ECON_FORBIDDEN`
  - UI should show internal-only messaging and link to access request channel

### Audit logging
We need auditable evidence for:
1) Access attempts to the dashboard (success + denied)
2) Administrative changes to who can access (flag allowlist changes and RBAC grants)

Proposed events (names aligned to existing audit convention):
- `audit.console.unit_econ.access_granted`
- `audit.console.unit_econ.access_denied`
- `audit.authz.permission_grant` / `audit.authz.permission_revoke` (existing if present; otherwise add scoped entries)
- `audit.flags.allowlist_update` (for `unit_econ_dashboard_internal`)

Event payload (keep minimal; avoid customer identifiers):
- actor_user_id, actor_email
- action, timestamp, request_id
- surface (ui|api), route
- outcome (granted|denied), reason (flag_off|missing_permission)
- ip / user_agent (if already standard)

Retention: follow standard internal audit retention policy (reference Security). No additional retention requirements in this ticket.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] When flag OFF: all calls to unit econ endpoints return 403 with `UNIT_ECON_FORBIDDEN` + reason `flag_off`.
- [x] When flag ON but user missing permission: 403 with reason `missing_permission`.
- [x] When flag ON and permission present: access works for both UI and API.
- [x] Audit events emitted for granted + denied access (UI and API) with request_id.
- [x] Audit events emitted for allowlist / RBAC changes (or confirmed already covered by existing audit infra).
- [x] Smoke test in staging with Finance + Eng allowlisted; confirm no PII leakage in logs.

## Implementation notes
- Prefer server-side enforcement in the API layer (do not rely on UI hiding).
- Use existing `requirePermission()` middleware; add `requireFeatureFlag()` wrapper to ensure consistent error codes.
- Ensure caching layers do not bypass auth (e.g., cache keys include user/permission context or cache only post-auth).

## Open questions
- Do we need a separate permission for the reconciliation report vs the dashboard itself? (Finance asked for broad access eventually; start with single `view_internal`.)
- Should we log “view” events for every successful request? (We’ll log access-granted per request; if noisy, we can downsample later.)

## References
- PM access-control requirements: PM-487
- Dashboard endpoints: ENG-8427
- Console page: ENG-8428
- Security reviewer: Marcus Lin
